statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-34183 ("Unbounded Memory Growth in the QUIC PATH_CHALLENGE Handler", Moderate): the OpenSSL QUIC stack allocates a PATH_RESPONSE frame for every PATH_CHALLENGE frame it receives and frees it only when the peer acknowledges it, so a malicious peer that floods a QUIC client or server with PATH_CHALLENGE frames and never acknowledges the responses can exhaust its memory and cause a denial of service. OpenSSL 3.5 is affected and fixed in OpenSSL 3.5.7; the FIPS modules are not affected because the QUIC stack is outside the FIPS module boundary. https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260609.txt. Fix on the openssl-3.5 branch: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/7d06955ebe0ecf8adfd4c1e92018586da47ef9ac, first released in OpenSSL 3.5.7. Alpine fixed it in openssl 3.5.7-r0: https://security.alpinelinux.org/vuln/CVE-2026-34183. The published DHI Alpine 3.23 builds from the openssl source (the main repository packages, and the openssl-fips FIPS-provider package in the DHI enterprise repository, built from the same source at matching versions from 3.5.5_git20260330-r1 on) are 3.5.4-r0, 3.5.5-r0, 3.5.5_git20260330-r1, 3.5.6-r0, 3.5.6-r1, 3.5.7-r0, 3.5.7-r1, 3.5.8-r0, 3.5.8-r1, 3.5.9-r0, 3.5.9-r1 and 3.5.9-r2, each on x86_64 and aarch64. The libcrypto in every one of these builds reports the OpenSSL release of its package version (3.5.5_git20260330-r1, a git snapshot dated 30 March 2026, reports 3.5.5). Builds before 3.5.7-r0 are based on OpenSSL 3.5.6 or earlier, and 3.5.7-r0 and every later build on OpenSSL 3.5.7 or later. The fix limits the PATH_CHALLENGE frames handled to one per received packet and lets the stack discard frames that need no acknowledgement, through three new libssl functions, ossl_quic_cfq_discard_unreliable(), ossl_quic_fifd_pkt_discard_unreliable() and ossl_ch_reset_rx_state(). All three are in the libssl symbol table of 3.5.7-r0 and every later build and absent from 3.5.4-r0, 3.5.5-r0, 3.5.5_git20260330-r1, 3.5.6-r0 or 3.5.6-r1, on both architectures (debug symbols from the openssl-dbg package of each build), while ossl_quic_cfq_new() and SSL_new() are present in every build. The openssl-fips package holds only the FIPS provider (fips.so, built from the same OpenSSL release as the package version in every build on both architectures) and its configuration files; the advisory places the QUIC stack outside the FIPS module boundary.

Fix on the openssl-3.5 branch: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/7d06955ebe0ecf8adfd4c1e92018586da47ef9ac, first released in OpenSSL 3.5.7. Debian's tracker lists it fixed for trixie in openssl 3.5.6-1~deb13u2: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-34183. The DHI Debian 13 openssl packages are rebuilds of Debian's trixie openssl, published in the DHI Debian repository and the DHI enterprise repository (the FIPS builds, and the openssl-provider-fips package of every build, only in the enterprise repository); the Debian changelog shipped in each libssl3t64 package shows which Debian release a build is based on. That changelog was read from every published build on amd64 and arm64: 25 versions, 17 standard and 8 FIPS builds, based on Debian 3.5.5-1~deb13u2, 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, 3.5.6-1~deb13u2, 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 and 3.5.9-1~deb13u1. No build based on Debian 3.5.5-1~deb13u2 or 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, FIPS builds included, names CVE-2026-34183. The first published rebuild of Debian 3.5.6-1~deb13u2, the fixed boundary here, and every later build, FIPS builds included, carry Debian's 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 entry naming it. The fix limits the PATH_CHALLENGE frames handled to one per received packet and lets the stack discard frames that need no acknowledgement, through three new libssl functions, ossl_quic_cfq_discard_unreliable(), ossl_quic_fifd_pkt_discard_unreliable() and ossl_ch_reset_rx_state(). All three are in the libssl symbol table of every build from the first rebuild of Debian 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 on, FIPS builds included, and absent from every earlier build, on both architectures (debug symbols from the libssl3t64-dbgsym package of each build), while ossl_quic_cfq_new() and SSL_new() are present in every build. Of the FIPS providers, the openssl-provider-fips package, read from every build on both architectures, ships the OpenSSL 3.1.2 FIPS provider in the FIPS builds and the FIPS provider from the build's own OpenSSL release (3.5.5, 3.5.6, 3.5.7 or 3.5.9) in the other builds; the advisory places the QUIC stack outside the FIPS module boundary, and the FIPS builds' libcrypto and libssl are Debian's 3.5 libraries checked above.
